title: Absolute deviation and variance for sign-valued variables
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$. Then the expected absolute deviation from the mean equals the expected squared deviation from the mean:
\[\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[|f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y)|\bigr]=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}\bigl[(f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}f(y))^2\bigr].\]
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
